feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/content/platform roles. Writing is polished and professional, but the document is somewhat repetitive and would be stronger with sharper outcomes, tighter structure, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good strategic/technical blend: combines communications leadership with Drupal, analytics, workflow design, and multimedia execution.  
- Strong use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and tool stack references add impact and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve focus and save space.  
- Add more outcome-based achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement”); standardize punctuation in lists and hyphenation such as “organization-wide” vs. other compounds. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete signals of scale, and less repetition of skills already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Replace broad lists with a tighter value proposition tied to recent work: enterprise web modernization, cross-channel strategy, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ page Drupal migration or 3.5M annual page views) to increase impact.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, enterprise web modernization, and content operations, including leading a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views. Strong in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “workflow/systems” repeat heavily across Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication”; “Web platform governance” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Reduce overlap and group related ideas for clarity. Suggested version: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS modernization • Editorial workflow & content operations • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow systems architecture • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Keep style consistent: use plural nouns where appropriate (“communications,” “insights”) and parallel phrasing throughout.
- Consider ordering by relevance/recency: strategy, web/platforms, operations, analytics, stakeholder/advocacy, multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeats Soft Skills and header language.
- “Digital strategy,” “workflow,” “analytics,” and “multimedia” are already covered in Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten around 3–4 signature contributions and add outcomes or scope where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise the National Association of Counties on enterprise web strategy, digital governance, campaign platforms, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-oriented line: “Improved cross-channel communications operations by refining digital workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Recast Drupal/CMS work to emphasize deliverables: “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, users served, teams enabled, publishing time reduced, search relevance improved, or engagement gains from campaigns/search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording overlaps heavily with the prior NACo roles on governance, analytics, and digital operations; emphasize consulting scope and new initiatives instead.
- AI search and microsite work are already echoed in “Recent Projects,” so keep this entry higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and operational scale-up.”
- Combine and streamline channel bullets; prioritize the biggest wins: website migration, analytics stack, studio build, governance. Move audience figures into one concise bullet.
- Add outcome language where possible: site performance, publishing efficiency, reporting speed, production cost/time savings, stakeholder adoption, or engagement growth.
- Example rewrite: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers; expanded analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery; built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio; and formalized governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role’s newsletter/social/video management.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older entries unless framed here as scaling via the in-house studio.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, cadence, and systems introduced.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to foreground scope and function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: newsletters, advocacy video, and cross-team planning. Example: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: add open rates, audience growth, production volume, turnaround time, or workflow improvements if available.
- Replace softer phrasing like “helped improve” and “helping establish” with stronger ownership verbs: “standardized,” “launched,” “expanded,” “streamlined,” “institutionalized.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and footer project; clarify this role as scaling/formalizing the series rather than starting it.
- “Editorial coordination/workflows” overlaps with the Director role; keep this entry focused on execution and operational management, not governance.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript/jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to the most recent roles, this item should either sharpen that emphasis or be trimmed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Rephrase to show level/relevance, not just names: **Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put the most relevant platform first and consider dropping weaker/older tools if space is tight; Drupal is clearly the anchor based on recent experience.
- Standardize naming for polish: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of just “Power Pages.”
- If you want more impact, add a qualifier in the section title: **Web Platforms & CMS Administration** or **Web Platforms & CMS Ecosystems**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or using one section for platforms and the other for implementation skills.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Reorder by relevance/recency: JavaScript • HTML/CSS • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery
- Tighten phrasing by collapsing versions: use “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”
- If space allows, add light context to show level: “JavaScript (front-end implementation), API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This substantially duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider keeping detail here and shortening the Topline version.
- jQuery may date the profile if given equal weight; place it last or remove unless it is still actively used.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow/systems” claims elsewhere. Make it more selective and grouped around automation impact, not collaboration apps.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to emphasize systems/automation tools first, and separate project-management/collaboration platforms.
- Cut lower-value/general tools if space is tight; Slack, Teams, and possibly Basecamp/Trello add little differentiation.
- Suggested rewrite: Automation & Workflow Systems: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana | Workflow automation, editorial planning, project tracking, and cross-team coordination
- If accurate, add scale/context elsewhere or in a cover note: e.g., “used to support multi-team publishing workflows” or “organization-wide planning systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap with general coordination already covered in Core Competencies and work experience.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the scale/strategic email work shown in recent NACo roles. Strengthen it by signaling CRM/email automation capability without repeating newsletter details already covered in experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Audience segmentation • Journey automation**
- If accurate, replace generic capability terms with stronger specifics: **list management, template deployment, A/B testing, deliverability, performance reporting**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or channel leadership language here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience
- “Engagement Systems” overlaps slightly with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep this item focused on email/CRM tools, not general ops tools

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with concrete outputs rather than leadership language that is better reserved for 2018–2024 roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and production impact: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital communications function.”
- Add specific scope/results if available: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, video cadence, email/social support, or audience/reach metrics.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with actions such as “supported,” “produced,” “coordinated,” “streamlined.”
- Possible version: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital communications team. Supported a major website refresh, coordinated web/email/social publishing, and produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates. Also provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on setup/production, not ongoing operations leadership.
- Avoid repeating website leadership claims already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Tighten it around distinctive contributions—especially the first podcast—and add any scale or outputs if available.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize unique impact: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Make the podcast the lead differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer outcome: “Produced digital and multimedia content to translate research and policy work into member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add 1 metric: number of episodes, projects supported, stakeholders served, or content pieces produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support and the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating “first” multimedia milestones here if stronger, more recent “firsts” already appear above.
